graphEvents.label: openhuman-full crates and TUI versus openhuman-main
terminal restore needs a panic hook, not only a Drop guard

label: openhuman-full adds no TUI crate over openhuman-main (the trees are identical); it adds the 417M of vendored TinyHumans crate sources that openhuman-main leaves empty, path-linked from its root manifest
openhuman-tui makes terminal ownership panic-safe with a Drop guard plus a chained panic hook that restores the alternate screen and raw mode, a requirement the 003 hardening child does not carry
openhuman-tui bounds runtime text in the reducer with a char-boundary-safe clip and an explicit [preview truncated] marker; the plan clips by display width with no marker
openhuman-tui coalesces redraws (100 ms input poll, 16 ms draw gate, 120 ms spinner); the plan redraws per event and polls verbs on a 5 s timer
the plan sanitizer is a replacement rule while the reference safe_text is a filter that keeps newlines, so the reference is not copyable as written for single-line rows

tinysecurity carries a four-way approval decision Once/Tool/Flow/Deny plus per-origin TTL bands of 180 s and 600 s and a human-only-tool bar; the plan refuses standing grants but names no maximum answer age
tinysecurity parses a channel reply as intent only, bounded at 4096 bytes, and never as execution authority; the plan answer path has no size bound and no intent-only statement
tinymemory models memory as a namespace tree with a Reach/inherit read rule and a provenance policy that treats unknown namespaces as untrusted; the plan shared plus per-bot files carry neither
